items.followUp: State the elastic limit of a spring and explain what happens when it is stretched beyond this limit.

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies the recovery condition.
rubric.description: States that the object returns to its original shape when the force is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this condition.

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies the limit of elastic behaviour.
rubric.description: Defines the elastic limit as the greatest force or stress for which the object still returns to its original shape.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying this maximum limit.

modelAnswer: The elastic limit is the maximum force or stress up to which a body returns to its original shape and size when the force is removed.
Beyond the elastic limit, the body does not completely regain its original shape.
A body is within its elastic limit when it recovers its original shape after the deforming force is removed.
What is meant by Elastic Limit?

items.followUp: A metal block has a mass of 2 kg and a volume of 0.001 m³. Find its density.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of density.
rubric.description: Defines density as mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Checks the SI unit of density.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit as kilogram per cubic metre.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct unit.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
Its SI unit is kilogram per cubic metre (kg m⁻³).

items.followUp: Define heat and temperature, and state one unit used to measure temperature.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of heat as energy transferred between bodies at different temperatures.
rubric.description: States that heat is energy that flows from a hotter body to a colder body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct meaning of heat.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of temperature.
rubric.description: Defines temperature as the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct meaning of temperature.

modelAnswer: Heat is a form of energy that flows from a hotter body to a colder body.
Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.

items.followUp: A car moving at 8 m s⁻¹ accelerates uniformly at 0.5 m s⁻² for 20 s. Find its distance travelled and final velocity.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the initial velocity, acceleration and time in SI units.
rubric.description: Records the given quantities, including converting half a minute to 30 s.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the data and time.

rubric.why: Checks use of the displacement equation and the calculated distance.
rubric.description: Uses s = ut + ½at² and obtains a distance of 390 m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the formula and substitution, and 1 mark for the correct distance with unit.

rubric.why: Checks use of the velocity equation and the calculated final velocity.
rubric.description: Uses v = u + at and obtains a final velocity of 16 m s⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the formula and substitution, and 1 mark for the correct final velocity with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 10 m s⁻¹, a = 0.2 m s⁻², t = ½ minute = 30 s.
Distance: s = ut + ½at².
Final velocity: v = u + at.

items.followUp: Resolve a force of 80 N acting at 60° to the x-axis into its perpendicular components.

rubric.why: Checks the correct resolution formula and horizontal component setup.
rubric.description: Uses Fx = F cos θ for the x-component.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct x-component formula and substitution.

rubric.why: Checks the calculated horizontal component.
rubric.description: Obtains Fx ≈ 43.3 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct x-component with unit.

rubric.why: Checks the correct vertical component setup.
rubric.description: Uses Fy = F sin θ for the y-component.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct y-component formula and substitution.

rubric.why: Checks the calculated vertical component.
rubric.description: Obtains Fy = 25 N.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct y-component with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 50 N, θ = 30° to the x-axis.
Horizontal component: Fx = F cos θ = (50 N) cos 30° = 43.3 N.
Vertical component: Fy = F sin θ = (50 N) sin 30° = 25 N.
The perpendicular components are 43.3 N along the x-axis and 25 N along the y-axis.

items.followUp: Define Young’s modulus and derive its expression in terms of force, original length, cross-sectional area and extension.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of Young’s modulus.
rubric.description: States that Young’s modulus is the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain, within the elastic limit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct ratio and elastic-limit condition.

rubric.why: Checks the expression for tensile stress.
rubric.description: Writes stress = force / cross-sectional area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct stress expression.

rubric.why: Checks the expression for tensile strain.
rubric.description: Writes strain = extension / original length.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct strain expression.

rubric.why: Checks the derived formula.
rubric.description: Derives Y = FL/(AΔL).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final expression.

modelAnswer: Young’s modulus is the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain, provided the material is within its elastic limit.
Tensile stress = force / cross-sectional area = F/A.
Tensile strain = extension / original length = ΔL/L.
Young’s modulus, Y = stress / strain = (F/A)/(ΔL/L) = FL/(AΔL).

items.followUp: What does the prefix milli- mean? Give one example of a unit that uses it.

rubric.why: Checks the role of prefixes in expressing multiples or submultiples of units.
rubric.description: States that a prefix is placed before a unit to indicate a multiple or fraction of that unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition.

rubric.why: Checks that the student can give a valid prefix example and its meaning.
rubric.description: Gives a correct prefix example, such as kilo = 10³ or milli = 10⁻³.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example with its meaning.

modelAnswer: A prefix is a symbol or name placed before a unit to show a multiple or submultiple of that unit.
For example, kilo- means 10³; 1 kilometre = 10³ metres.

items.followUp: Convert 12 years into seconds, taking 1 year as 365 days.

rubric.why: Checks the conversion of years into seconds using the number of days, hours, minutes and seconds.
rubric.description: Uses 1 year = 365 days, 1 day = 24 hours, 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversion factors and setup.

rubric.why: Checks the final converted age.
rubric.description: Obtains 473,040,000 seconds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: age = 15 years; 1 year = 365 days.
Time = 15 years × 365 days/year × 24 hours/day × 60 minutes/hour × 60 seconds/minute.
